entities.summary:
Francesco Salviati, Archbishop of Pisa from 1474 until his death on May 14, 1478, was a central figure in the tumultuous political landscape of 15th-century Florence, whose ambition led him to participate in one of the most audacious plots against the powerful Medici family. His involvement in the Pazzi conspiracy of 1478 underscores the fierce rivalries and papal intrigues that characterized the Italian Renaissance, highlighting the precarious balance of power between leading aristocratic families and the papacy in shaping the destiny of city-states. Salviati's role, particularly in recruiting mercenary forces, cemented his place in history as a clerical orchestrator of political violence aimed at overthrowing established rule.

Appointed Archbishop of Pisa in 1474, a position fiercely contested by the Medici, Salviati became a key conspirator alongside Francesco de' Pazzi and Jacopo de' Pazzi, with covert backing from Pope Sixtus IV. The conspiracy's objective was the assassination of Lorenzo and Giuliano de' Medici during Easter mass on April 26, 1478, within Florence Cathedral. While Giuliano was murdered, Lorenzo de' Medici survived the attack, rallying popular support against the conspirators. Salviati's specific task was to seize the Palazzo della Signoria, the seat of Florentine government, but his attempt was thwarted by the resolute resistance of the Florentine priori.
